description.narrative: Overall objective: To mitigate the immediate impact of the COVID-19 crisis in Mongolia and support national health systems in the medium and long-term. Specific objective 1: To strengthen capacity of national health systems to monitor, prevent, and control the spread and effects of COVID-19. Specific objective 2: To improve quality of laboratories service delivery; Specific objective 3: To improve accessibility and quality of essential health care logistics and services.

Now this team planned to facilitate how to manage hospital beds and monitor home treatment in local level. Home deaths and waiting time to hospitalization were reduced.

comment.narrative: The NCCD as the national reference laboratory confirms 3500 suspected samples sent from 9 districts and 13 provinces laboratories by PCR in the 2nd year of the project implementation in addition to 6 provincial laboratories reported in the first year.

Government has paid the attention to build laboratory capacity in sub national level and for establishing public health laboratory network for emerging infectious diseases. The number and capacity of PCR laboratories have been increased with 11 new molecular biology laboratories in Ulaanbaatar and 22 in rural areas have been established respectively during the project implementation period.

Procurement of communications materials for health workers and local communities on nonpharmaceutical interventions.
Type of communications materials developed:1. Press release2. News release3. IEC material set for the public4. IEC material set for HCWs

comment.narrative: FOUR TYPEs OF COMMUNICATION MATERIALS PRESS RELEASE 3 NEWS RELESAE 8IEC MATERIAL SET FOR PUBLIC 9IEC MATERIAL SET FOR HCWs 6

The European Union and the WHO have actively supported Mongolias health system through several initiatives from 2021 to 2023. In 2021 a series of handover ceremonies transferred essential medical equipment to Mongolia alongside training in laboratory capacity building and essential health services. These initiatives continued in 2022 under the MCCR project with four press releases on implementation activities covering skills enhancement and healthcare improvements. In 2023 results of these efforts were disseminated in a workshop. Across these years WHO social platforms highlighted these milestones while numerous Information Education and Communication IEC materials were developed targeting both the public and healthcare workers to reinforce proper protective equipment usage and hygiene practices.

Number of health facilities reporting multisource surveillance data on a daily basis

comment.narrative: All level health care facilities collecting and reporting health care capacity bed utilization surveillance and resources data on daily basis. Decision makers have unified information on all geographical locations level situations and resources. In the past reports were usually monthly. The use of multisource surveillance data has made it possible to conduct transmission stage assessments in each local level and to plan responses and nonpharmaceutical measures based on realtime data and real situations assessments which is one of the important achievements of our work.

comment.narrative: 9 districts and 21 provinces departments of health started to analyze health care capacity data to monitor health utilization. As result of this analyze and WPRO guidance established Bed management team established by MoH order No.595 on 2021 in Ulaanbaatar. Now this team planned to facilitate how to manage hospital beds and monitor home treatment in local level. Home deaths and waiting time to hospitalization were reduced.

comment.narrative: 112218 women at reproductive age 1549 are benefitted from improved delivery services at BaynUlgii Bulgan GobiAltai Dundgobi Uvurkhangai Sukhbaatar and Uvurkhangai provinces. 7650 children under 5 in 18 remote soums subprovinces of BaynUlgii Bulgan GobiAltai Dundgobi Uvurkhangai Sukhbaatar and Uvurkhangai provinces are benefitted from improved young children services. 51119 people or all age groups of people in remote 5 soums of Baynkhongor Gobisumber Khovd and Zavkhan provinces and in two periurban areas in Nalaikh district are benefitted from integrated PHC services including MCH NCD CD and elderly care.
